messages.body_plain:
Thanks for filing the issue!

In the meantime, here is a simple R implementation of the function:

 as.csv <- function(df) {
    sapply(1:nrow(df), function(row.index)
       paste(df[row.index,], collapse=","))
 }

 df <- data.frame(x=1:12,y=(1:12)*2)
 writeLines(as.csv(df), con = "test.csv")

messages.subject: Backend support
messages.body_plain:
I am sure this is a dumb question....

Out of the box, when I do a read.csv, run some R processing, then perform a write.csv.

is renjin reading the CSV into memory to perform calculations? or is this loading into the file system to perform calculations.

Also, is it possible to configure renjin to use a FS, Database,  redis, or another datastore?

Thanks!

messages.subject: Re: Backend support
messages.body_plain:
If you use read.csv, the csv file is being loaded into memory, and then the calculations performed.

You can provide your own implementations of DoubleVector or StringVector to provide different storage for the data. This is an area we're in the early phases of exploring, mostly because for it to be useful, you have to be able to avoid lots of intermediary structures; otherwise you end up with (some form of) the data in memory anyway.
More info here: http://www.renjin.org/blog/2013-07-30-deep-dive-vector-pipeliner.html

We've built a few backends like this for specific datasets that we work with for clients, but we haven't yet built anything generic.

What is the shape of your data? Where does it live?

Alex

Hello,

Is it possible to use R SPARQL library with Renjin?

Thanks,
Prasad

messages.subject: Re: Using R SPARQL Library with Renjin
messages.subject_clean: Using R SPARQL Library with Renjin
messages.body_plain:
No, unfortunately it is not. The SPARQL package on CRAN depends on the XML and RCurl packages, both of which are not available in Renjin.

We plan to provide XML and RCurl packages specifically for Renjin at some point in time, but I can not give you a date at this moment.

Maarten-Jan
